title: optimize NCCL collectives, KV-cache prefetching and continuous batching for tensor-parallel (TP) multi-GPU
author: Maya Chen
body:
Motivation: On multi-GPU tensor-parallel configurations we observed suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local kernel execution as model context lengths and KV-cache pressure increased. This manifested as higher p95/p99 latency and reduced throughput for long-chat and streaming workloads. This PR combines targeted NCCL stream/priority tuning, lower sync ingress points for kernel scheduling, KV-cache prefetch/eviction heuristics, and continuous-batching adaptive thresholds to improve overlap and reduce tail latency.

Summary of changes: 1) Assign collectives to dedicated NCCL CUDA streams with explicit stream priorities based on collective size (small allreduce -> medium priority, large allreduce/allgather -> higher priority) and per-device stream pools to avoid head-of-line blocking. 2) Introduce non-blocking enqueue for collective coordination: control-plane synchronization moved off the critical token path and uses atomic flags + callbacks to trigger dependent kernels rather than cudaDeviceSynchronize. 3) Add lightweight kernel-fusion points for KV-cache scatter/gather + small GEMM kernels to reduce kernel-launch overhead for short sequences. 4) Implement KV-cache prefetching for expected next-token ranges during continuous batching; prefetch is opportunistic and cancels on eviction/backpressure. 5) Adaptive continuous-batching flush: dynamic flush thresholds based on observed latency SLOs, model sequence-length histogram, and current GPU utilization to balance throughput/latency. 6) Improve error handling and graceful fallback: if NCCL stream allocation fails or a collective hangs, fall back to a conservative single-stream rendezvous with instrumentation.

Benchmarks: On internal 8xA100 TP tests with a 4k context chat workload: throughput improvement 8-18% (depending on model size and sequence distribution) and p95/p99 latency reduced by 12-28%. KV-heavy workloads improved more (up to 30% lower p99) due to prefetch + fused kernels. Microbench harness and end-to-end load tests are included.

Compatibility: Changes are backward compatible at API level. Default behavior conservatively preserves previous stream assignment; the new policy is enabled behind a runtime flag (env REDWOOD_TP_NCCL_OPT=1) and gated on driver/cuDNN/NCCL minimum versions.

Checklist: - [x] Performance tests added to perf-canary harness - [x] Unit tests for new scheduling primitives - [x] Integration test for multi-GPU KV-cache correctness - [x] Feature gated behind env flag and runtime version checks - [x] Docs note in CHANGELOG/ops runbook

Risk: Medium. The most sensitive part is NCCL stream scheduling across devices; we added extensive telemetry and auto-fallback to reduce blast radius.

Notes: This PR follows up on prior NCCL overlap tuning work (see ENG-2147) and pairs with continuous-batching changes in ENG-2201.

review_comments: Alejandro Ruiz: Can you add a short explanation of how stream priorities map to collective size? I want to make sure we don't starve small collectives.
Maya Chen: Added mapping table and a comment in stream_pool.cc; small collectives use mid-priority and are allowed fast-paths, large collectives get higher priority to reduce overall wait time.
Priya Natarajan: Please add a perf run showing end-to-end p99 under a realistic chat mix (short+long contexts). Also include a playback of the fallback path once.
Maya Chen: Added perf-canary harness config and attached run summary to the PR; fallback path exercised in CI simulation (see integration logs).
Evan McDonald: Lgtm after addressing the telemetry labels and adding the version gates.
changed_files_snippet: serving/runtime/nccl/stream_pool.cc: added stream priority allocation and per-device pool (approx 230 LOC)
serving/runtime/kv_cache/prefetcher.cc: new prefetch path + cancelation hooks (approx 180 LOC)
merge_commit: Squashed commit into main: optimize NCCL collectives and TP batching (merged by Alejandro Ruiz)
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and tail latency via NCCL stream prioritization, KV-cache prefetching and adaptive continuous-batching. Feature is gated behind REDWOOD_TP_NCCL_OPT and requires NCCL >= 2.14.
notes_for_ops: Enable REDWOOD_TP_NCCL_OPT in staging for 48h canary; monitor tp_collective_latency and kvcache_miss_rate. If collective hangs observed, unset the flag to fallback to legacy single-stream path.
perf_results_summary: 8-18% throughput improvement on 8xA100 TP for long-context chat; up to 30% p99 improvement for KV-heavy workloads. Detailed numbers in perf-canary artifact.
